story_arc: India faces the largest oil supply shock in history.
It peaked at $156 per barrel. The rupee hit an all-time low.
22 ships are stranded. Mines make the strait impassable for months.
Crude is manageable. Cooking gas is rationed for 330 million households.
Even a ceasefire signed March 28 cannot reopen the strait until summer.
—— Your refinery ——
MRPL already shut its crude unit. Your supply window is closing.
Jamnagar runs at full complexity. Single-source refineries are bleeding cash.
The government has overridden your product slate. LPG comes first.
—— Your balance sheet ——
You are losing over fifty rupees on every litre of diesel you sell.
The Russia waiver expires April 3. Your cheapest fallback vanishes in ten days.
Brent is at $100 today. It may not be this low again.
—— Your government ——
Delhi is rationing, escorting, and freezing prices. It expects months, not weeks.
Non-alignment got four ships through. That diplomatic capital is finite.
Fertilizer gas is already cut to seventy percent. Kharif is at risk.
—— Your board ——
The annual import bill has surged by over a hundred billion dollars.
Three deadlines converge before April 6. Your board is planning for none of them.
—— What everyone else is missing ——
Markets priced in a ceasefire. Mine clearance alone takes eight to twelve weeks.
You have ten days before your fallback disappears. Decide now.
